## Session 2026-10-01 — A document's figures show their images in the reader and in PDF, Word and HTML exports, fetched with the volume and removed with it; "[Figure]" prints only when the image is absent, a film links to its page, and a space between two inline elements is drawn (lane READ; #1516, one fold-in)

**The question.** Lane READ of the 2026-09-28 plan of record, owner decision D3 option (f)4. A figure printed only its file's name — "figure_1162" in the reader, "[figure_1162]" in a PDF, "[Figure: figure_1162]" in Word — and neither its head nor its captions, and the app had no image to show. The lane: fetch each volume's figure images from history.state.gov beside its XML (never a page's scan), remove them with the volume, count them in Volumes & Storage, draw them in the reader and embed them in PDF and Word; treat a figure's head and paragraphs as captions with no re-index; print "[Figure]" only when the image is absent and nothing for an empty `<figure/>`; give the 20 Public Diplomacy films a "Watch on history.state.gov ↗" link and their head; and, folded in, stop the reader dropping the whitespace between two inline elements (`frus1861` d2 read "Washington,February 28, 1861"). And measure the real corpus image total.

**What was measured** (corpus `8e5da08c1`, the 553 manifest volumes, 2026-10-01; the scripts and their output are in the session's folder outside the repository, `durable/w49/work/READ/`).
- **The image total.** By HEAD request to `https://static.history.state.gov/frus/<volume>/<url>.png` for each of the 968 distinct (volume, `<graphic url>`) pairs the figures name (`measure_images.py`; no image was fetched there — review round 1 read each served image's first 24 bytes, below): **553 are served, 140,994,857 bytes (141.0 MB, 134.5 MiB), in 96 volumes**, every one as `image/png`; 415 answer **HTTP 403**, which is what the host says for a file it does not have. Of the 415, 402 are title-page figures (one in each of 402 volumes; none is served) and **13** are names in the text: `Appendix A.1`–`A.3` in `frus1917-72PubDipv06` and again in `v07`, `figure_0283` and `figure_0318` in `frus1945Malta`, `figure_1163` in `frus1946v01`, `figure_0284` and `figure_0285` in `frus1950-55Intel`, `figure_0001` in `frus1952-54v04`, and `genassemblybldg` in `frus1969-76ve09p1`. Per volume that has a served image: median 328,492.5 bytes (the mean of the 48th and 49th of the 96; this entry first gave 337,027, the 49th), mean 1,468,696, the largest `frus1943CairoTehran` at 25,443,143; the largest single image is its `figure_0383.png`, 3,556,499 bytes. In documents alone: 486 names, 480 served, 112,077,086 bytes. `.png` is added to every name, whatever it ends in: `OpenPitMine.jpg` is served only as `OpenPitMine.jpg.png`.
- **The figures.** 1,035 `<figure>`s: 532 in a `<div type="document">` (426 a graphic alone, 50 a head and a graphic, 32 a graphic and paragraphs, 20 empty, 2 a `figDesc` and a graphic, 1 paragraphs alone, 1 a head and paragraphs) and 503 outside one: 403 on title pages, one in each of 403 volumes (402 name a graphic; `frus1865p4`'s is an empty `<figure/>`, which is why the title pages give 402 names); 20 video players; and 80 elsewhere — 45 in `section` divs, 33 in `chapter` or `subchapter` divs, and 2 directly in `<front>`, outside every div (`frus1931-41v02` `figure_0007`, served, 284,620 bytes; `frus1952-54v04` `figure_0001`, one of the 13 refused). No figure names two graphics.
- **A page's scan is a `<graphic>` too.** 1,143,043 of them, in `<facsimile><surface>`, in 551 of the 553 volumes (`scan_graphics.py`), against 992 in figures and none anywhere else. So "the figures' graphics" is not "the graphics", and the name scan takes a `<graphic>` only inside a `<figure>`. A first draft of the doc comment said a scan was a `<pb facs>` and no `<graphic>`; the fixture now carries the real `<surface>` shape.
- **The films.** 20 video figures (`scan_videos.py`): 12 `<object>` players in `frus1917-72PubDip` (appendix-5 and appendix-11), 5 `<iframe>`s in volume VI (appendix-1 to -3) and 3 in volume VII (appendix-1 to -3; these three have no head). Every one sits in an `online-supplement` div inside a `section`/`historical-document` the parser promotes to a document. The eight pages their links name each answered HTTP 200, and an invented `appendix-zzz` 404.
- **The whitespace.** 54,025 whitespace-only runs between two inline elements inside documents (`scan_seams.py`): 14,193 a `<placeName>` then a `<date>` in a dateline, in 9,884 documents; 4,439 a `<gloss>` then a `<persName>` in a paragraph. 7,337 more follow a `<note>` before an inline element, and 6,387 have a `<pb>` on one side and an inline element on the other.

**What changed.**
- **Fetch, keep, remove, count** (`DownloadManager.swift`, `DownloadModels.swift`, `ResetService.swift`, `FRUSExplorerApp.swift`). When a download finishes, `DownloadManager` scans the volume's XML for the graphics of its figures outside the title page (`FigureImageLibrary.graphicNames`) and fetches each into `{Volumes}/<volume>.figures/<url>.png`, dropping any image an update's text no longer names. A 403 or 404 is remembered for the session and not asked for again; a failed transfer, an error status, or a 2xx that is not a PNG (a network's sign-in page) is not kept and is asked for again. Requests follow Allow Cellular Downloads. A whole-volume run is keyed by the volume and which of its texts it read, so an update that lands mid-run stops the old text's names and starts a run over the new one; an image that lands after its volume was removed is removed. `deleteVolume`, `cancelDownload` and Reset Local Data remove the folder. `storageReport` counts the images per volume and in total; `StorageReport.totalVolumesBytes` stays the XML alone, because the index estimate is derived from it.
- **A volume downloaded before this build** is brought up to its images by a pass over the library at launch and on reconnect (`DownloadManager.fetchMissingFigureImages(among:)`, added in review round 1, below; as first committed, such a volume got an image only when the reader or an export asked for one). Until the pass reaches a volume, the reader and the PDF, Word and HTML exports fetch the image they need (`FigureImageStore`, one per process, configured at boot): a catalogue volume's only, and only while online (`FigureImageStore.mayFetch`). The first image fetched that way starts the rest of the volume's.
- **Volumes & Storage** (`SettingsComponents.swift`, `StorageHubModel.swift`, both hubs). The storage bar has a **Figures** segment after XML; a volume's row shows its text and images together; Free Up Space's estimate adds the images once, outside the 2.8× index factor.
- **The figure itself** (`FRUSRenderNode.swift`, `ASTToRenderNodeConverter.swift`). `.figureBlock` carries a `FigureBlock`: the image's name and volume, the head (a second head on a line of its own), each `<p>` and `figDesc` as a caption line, and for a video player its page's address. An empty figure converts to nothing. A player's own elements and hidden text print nothing.
- **The reader** (`FRUSRenderNodeHTMLSerializer.swift`, `HTMLTemplate.swift`, `FRUSURLSchemeHandler.swift`). A figure is a `<figure>` — a `<span>` inside a line, so a paragraph is not split — holding its head, an `<img src="frusexplorer://figure/<volume>/<file>">` and its captions. The scheme handler answers with the bytes, or fails at once so the placeholder shows, fetches the image, and then has the page ask again; the page's second request starts no fetch of its own. "[Figure]" is shown only while the image is absent.
- **Exports** (`PDFCollectionExporter.swift`, `DocxCollectionExporter.swift`, `CollectionItemHTMLRenderer.swift`, `HTMLCollectionExporter.swift`, `CollectionContentResolver.swift`). A PDF, Word or HTML export first fetches the images its full-body documents lack; the live preview does not, nor — since review round 1 — a BibTeX, RIS or Zotero export, which prints none. PDF sets an image under its head at two pixels to the point, never wider than the 468 pt column or taller than 560 pt; Word stores it once as `word/media/figureN.png` and draws it in the paragraph under its head (a figure that is an image alone stays a run of its line, so a mark in a table cell stays in the cell; in a footnote the image prints as its placeholder, since the footnotes part has no relationship to it); HTML embeds it as a `data:` URL. A film prints its head and a link — in the PDF, the address in print.
- **No re-index, and no stale highlight.** A figure's head, captions and placeholder, and the drawn space below, are under `data-skip` in the page and are not flat text in either Swift walk, so `renderingVersion`, `body_hash` and `body_text` are what they were. **The index stays at v64.** The selection bridge (`kSelectionJS` and `frus-selection.js`, kept identical) treats a figure and a drawn space as drawn parts, so a selection that starts or ends on one still maps to offsets.
- **The fold-in** (`FRUSDocumentParser.swift`, `FRUSASTNode.swift`, `IndexingPipeline.swift`). The parser keeps a whitespace-only run as `.elementSpace` where the element before it is inline and the one after is not a block (`keepsElementSpace`): never directly inside a container that holds only blocks, and across a page break only when text precedes it. It is drawn as one space, outside the flat text; `PrintedText` skips it, because the index's printed join already spaced these seams and appending a space would move stored text.
- **Docs.** `CLAUDE.md` gains a Key Data Flows entry. Thirteen manual proposals under "READ — #1516" in `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md`. EditableContent: no block's text changes, 10 ranged blocks re-pointed, one Amendment-Log bullet.

**Decisions the plan did not settle.**
- **Where the files go:** `{Volumes}/<volume>.figures/`, a folder beside the XML, excluded from backup as the XML is. Everything that sweeps the volumes directory looks for `.xml` files, so the folder is none of theirs.
- **Title-page figures are not fetched or drawn.** All 403 sit outside every `<div>`, so in no document the parser returns, and the host serves none. The two figures directly in `<front>` are outside every `<div>` too, and the name scan, which leaves out only `<titlePage>`, does fetch those: see Still open.
- **A sign-in page is not a refusal.** A 2xx that is not a PNG is treated as a failed transfer and asked for again, where the first draft remembered it for the session: behind a captive portal that would have marked every image of the volume as missing until relaunch.
- **Side-loaded volumes** get images only when their id is a catalogue volume's (#777: the app has no address for any other).
- **The HTML export embeds images too.** The lane named PDF and Word; an HTML export that printed "[Figure]" beside them would have been the odd one.
- **Pre-download sizes do not count images.** A volume's stated size, the bulk download's total and onboarding's "≈ 3.5 GB" are the manifest's XML sizes (and match files); the manifest carries no image sizes. With images the whole series is 3,338,778,538 + 162,354,028 + 140,994,857 = 3,642,127,423 bytes, which rounds to 3.6 GB. Onboarding's figure is the owner's text and was left alone; see Still open.
- **Figures in footnotes** (6 in the corpus, all empty `<figure/>`s in `frus1881`) print nothing; an image in a Word footnote would print its placeholder.
- **The run bookkeeping was simplified during mutation testing.** Three checks removed a late image after its volume was gone; each survived alone, since the first does the work, and one of the others would have deleted the images of a volume removed and downloaded again mid-run (read from the code, not run). Two were deleted. Run-level de-duplication has no test: with per-image de-duplication under it, removing it changes no file and no request, only how often a volume's XML is scanned.

**How it was verified** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`; Xcode 27.0). 60 new tests in 9 suites: `FigureCaptionTests`, `ElementSpaceTests`, `FigureImageMarkupTests`, `ElementSpaceRuleTests`, `FigureExportTests`, `FigureImageExportTests`, `FigureImageDownloadTests`, `FigureStorageDisplayTests` and `FigureReaderTests`, the last in a real web view.
- **A/B on unfixed code.** The 13 tests that need no new API, built and run in a copy of `v2`'s tree at `dc17d945`: **"✘ Test run with 13 tests in 3 suites failed after 0.059 seconds with 27 issues"** — 12 failed; the 13th, that the drawn spaces are no flat text, holds on both sides by design and is killed by mutant batch 2.
- **A/B by mutation**, for the tests that cannot compile against `v2`: 68 mutants in 8 batches, applied and reverted as exact text edits by `mutate.py`, the tree checked clean after each. Batch 1 (reader, serializer, converter, parser, bridge): "✘ Test run with 58 tests in 10 suites failed … with 56 issues", 26 tests. Batch 2 (figure and space as flat text): 55 tests, 31 issues, 8 tests. Batch 2b (drawn outside `data-skip`): 36 tests, 28 issues, 5 tests. Batch 3 (exports, storage, manager): 29 tests, 34 issues, 17 tests. Batch 4: 42 tests, 22 issues, 14 tests. Batches 5–7, after the run rework, one mutant per expectation: 9 mutants and 9 tests; 6 and 5; 5 and 10. Of the 60 new tests every one fails in the unfixed run or under a mutant (`killed.py`).
- **Green.** The nine suites and `SelectionScriptParityTests`: **"✔ Test run with 63 tests in 10 suites passed after 4.099 seconds"**. Full unit target (`-only-testing FRUSExplorerTests`, on the final build, after every doc but this entry): **"✔ Test run with 6381 tests in 756 suites passed after 315.146 seconds"**, "** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **"; the test build's only warnings are the two known residues. `CodingStandardsAuditTests` and `EditableContentKeyTests` again with this entry in place: 80 tests in 2 suites passed.
- **One flake, fixed.** In the first run of a newly built test host, with twelve suites running, `FigureReaderTests`' caption-selection test timed out at the harness's 5 seconds ("the selection bridge posted nothing"); the next three runs passed. Its wait is now 20 seconds.
- **By eye, in the app** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, real volumes copied into the simulator; screenshots in the session's folder outside the repository, `durable/w49/work/READ/shots/`). `frus1951v03p1` d249 with a stand-in PNG in its figures folder: the image drawn at the column's width, in its shape, inside the editorial note. `frus1917-72PubDipv06` appendix-1: "[Figure]" for `Appendix A.1` (one of the 13 the host refuses), then "Online Video Supplement", "Reel 1" and "Watch on history.state.gov ↗". `frus1861` d2: "Washington, February 28, 1861."
- **macOS:** `FRUSExplorerMac` **"** BUILD SUCCEEDED **"** (Xcode 27.0, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, a clean build in the lane's own derived data, and an incremental one on the final tree), with no warning beyond the two known residues.

**Still open.**
- **By eye, owner.** On the Mac: a document with a figure (`frus1946v01` d587's maps, after the table), Volumes & Storage's Figures segment and a row's size, and a PDF and a Word export of that document. The Mac app was not run: a development build shares the owner's store. On an iPad nothing was run, and a real image from history.state.gov was never fetched, until review round 1 (below): every transfer in the tests is injected, and this entry's by-eye image was a stand-in.
- **The images' bytes were not read** by the survey, which was HEAD requests; a file served as `image/png` that is not a PNG would fail the app's signature check, print "[Figure]" and be asked for again. Closed in review round 1: all 553 open with the PNG signature.
- **Onboarding's "≈ 3.5 GB"** (`OnboardingView.swift:609`) and the manuals' corpus size are 141 MB short of a full download now. The owner's text; not changed.
- **`body_text` of the 12 `frus1917-72PubDip` film sections** holds the player's hidden text and script (`298x530`, `brightcove.createExperiences();`), because the index walks a figure's children. Fixing it changes stored text and needs an index version; read from the code, not from an index.
- **An image in flight when an update drops its name** is stored after the update's run has pruned, and stays until the volume's next update or removal.
- **Two things read in passing, not verified:** `DownloadManager.cancelDownload` removes the XML at the destination even when it cancels an Update of a volume already on the device; and `PDFCollectionExporter.drawFrameWithHighlights` takes line origins from `CTFrameGetLineOrigins` without adding the frame path's origin, which the new image drawing does add.

**Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01).** Fifteen confirmed findings, all resolved in code, tests or this entry, and three of the four nits taken. The scripts and their output are in the session's folder outside the repository, `durable/w49/work/READ/r1/`.
- **The installed base had no images, and a failed fetch was never tried again** (correctness; a deviation from D3). The fetch started only from a finished download and from the first image the reader or an export asked for, so a library downloaded before build 49 had none until a figure was looked at while online, and a transfer that failed, or a run cut short, was never resumed. `DownloadManager.fetchMissingFigureImages(among:)` is a pass over the catalogue volumes on the device, in id order, one at a time; the app starts it at launch and each time the device comes back online, once downloads are resumed (`FRUSExplorerApp.fetchMissingFigureImages(with:appState:)`). A volume whose run ended with nothing failed is recorded in `{Volumes}/.figure-images-complete.json` against its XML's size and modification date, so the library's XML is read once and not at every launch; whatever replaces the file changes the stamp. The pass stops when the manager is suspended and after three volumes in a row whose transfers all fail, so a launch that cannot fetch (offline, or cellular with Allow Cellular Downloads off) does not read the whole library to find that out. Side-loaded volumes are not read. The reader's and the exports' fetch of one image stays, for a volume the pass has not reached.
- **BibTeX, RIS and the Zotero send fetched images they never print** (correctness). The fetch was keyed on `purpose == .export` alone. `ExportFormat.printsFigureImages` is true for PDF, Word and HTML only; the export sheet passes it to `resolve(…printsFigureImages:)`, and `resolveDocuments` (RIS, Zotero) never fetches. The fetch moved out of `loadBatchContext` to one place after the items are resolved, so the smart and the static path cannot be wired apart, and it asks only for the images of documents resolved at full body depth. While it asks, the export sheet's status line reads "Fetching figure images…" (a new string, `collection.export.status.fetchingFigures`), and `FigureImageStore.fetchAbsent` stops between images when its task is cancelled.
- **The real host, an iPad, and real exports** (correctness, test gap). Three things were run. (1) **Every served image's first 24 bytes** were read by range request (`read_signatures.py`, 2026-10-01): all 553 answered 206 and open with the PNG signature, `OpenPitMine.jpg.png` among them (500 by 378 pixels). Widths run 89 to 19,043 pixels (`frus1958-60v03mSupp` `eq_03.png`), heights 18 to 5,536 (`frus1946v01` `figure_1166.png`, 10,568 wide); 72 of the 553 are wider than 936 pixels — the PDF's 468 pt column and Word's 6.5 inches, at two pixels to the point — so 72 are scaled down in an export; the 13 taller than Word's 1,152 pixels are all among them. (2) **The app fetched real images on an iPad** (iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 26.5, `9F3D84A4`, 2026-10-02 00:03 EDT; the container saved first and put back afterwards): four real volumes cloned into the container, the app launched, and 13 seconds later the launch pass had stored `frus1946v01`'s 2 images (569,273 bytes), `frus1951v03p1`'s 15 (2,879,080) and `frus1958-60v03mSupp`'s 36 (7,926,523) — each total the HEAD survey's to the byte, all 53 files PNGs — made no folder for `frus1917-72PubDipv06`, whose three names the host refuses, and recorded all five volumes on the device complete. By eye: `frus1946v01` d587's Annex "A" facsimile under its title and above its table; `frus1951v03p1` d289's photographs, each over its caption with the name still a link; Volumes & Storage's bar with an orange **Figures 11.4 MB** segment between XML 34 MB and Index 33.5 MB, and the rows reading 10 MB and 12 MB where the XML alone is 9.4 and 9.1 (`shots/`). (3) **A PDF, a Word file and an HTML page were exported with those images** by a one-off test, not committed, that loaded d587, d289 and `frus1958-60v03mSupp` d444 through `DocumentViewModel` and ran the three exporters over the iPad's figures folder. The PDF's 15 pages, rendered to pixels and read: the facsimile, "[Figure]" for the refused `figure_1163`, the 10,568-pixel world map at the column's width, nine photographs over their captions, and d444's four equation images, the 19,043-pixel one at the column's width. The Word package passes `unzip -t`, holds 15 `word/media` parts each byte-identical to its fetched file, and draws them at most 6.50 by 4.58 inches (the map 6.50 by 3.40, the widest equation 6.50 by 0.27) with one placeholder; the HTML embeds 15 images and one placeholder. Not run: the Mac app, and Word itself — see Still open.
- **A late image moved a revealed footnote out of view** (correctness, and a comment that was no longer true). The reveal's comment said the page has no images. An image on the device is answered before `didFinish`, so layout is settled; one that is not is fetched and laid out after the reveal's scroll, and a map pushes the footnotes down by its height. The reveal now records the entry it brought the reader to (`FRUSURLSchemeHandler.revealedFootnoteGlobal`), the retry script brings it back into view when its image has loaded, and the reader's own wheel, touch, click or key forgets it first.
- **The privacy manifest** names `static.history.state.gov` among the public reads and says when the app asks it without being asked; its file-timestamp note names the stamp above. Whether the App Store Connect label needs a change is the owner's to confirm.
- **Tests that could not fail** (tests-claims; seven gaps, each closed by a test driving the code the gap named). The reader's own load (`FigureReaderTests.theReadersLoadNamesImagesByItsVolume`, through `DocumentViewModel.load` and a real web view); Word's fit-to-page clamp (`docxFitsALargeImage`, the corpus's widest and tallest images and two through the exporter); the export header's dateline (`theExportedDatelineKeepsItsSpace`, `frus1865p4` d493's own dateline through the resolver); a link in a caption or a figure's head (`aLinkInACaptionResolvesWhenTapped`, registered and dispatched); both storage hubs (`bothHubsCountTheImages`, a scan of each hub's bar and row); the smart-collection export and `cancelDownload` (`aSmartCollectionsExportFetchesAbsentImages`, `cancellingADownloadRemovesItsImages`); and the parser's left-hand clause (`ElementSpaceRuleTests.notKeptAfterABlock`: a block before, an inline element after).
- **The header's dateline is a smaller case than this entry implied.** `renderNodePlainText` feeds the header's dateline, which is read only from a dateline that is the document's own child. Measured (`scan_dateline_parents.py`): of the datelines holding a whitespace-only run between two inline elements, 43 are a document's own child, 13,692 sit in an `<opener>` (9,494 documents), 742 in a closer and 9 in an attachment. The opener's dateline prints with the body, where the space was already drawn.
- **Figures corrected above, in place:** the median (328,492.5 bytes; 337,027 was the upper middle value of 96), the title-page count (403 figures in 403 volumes, 402 of them naming a graphic), and what "80 in sections" holds. The same corrections are in `DownloadManager.swift`'s comments and in the Mac §5.1 proposal. `FigureImageStore`'s comment said a unit test's shared store has no image and fetches none, which was false in the test host, where the app's boot configured it over the simulator's own volumes and the network; the boot now leaves it unconfigured there and does not start the pass (`FigureImageStore.isUnitTestHost`), so the comment is true.
- **Nits taken.** `FigureBlock.videoURL`'s comment says all eight film pages answered 200 (asked again 2026-10-01: eight 200s, and `appendix-zzz` 404). The download tests' poll allows 20 seconds where it allowed 3, and `imageFetchedLaterIsDrawn`'s two polls 20 where they allowed 5. **Left:** the side-load notice (below) has no ⚑ box in `Docs/EditableContent/`: it is flagged here, in the Amendment-Log's bullet and in the side-loading proposal's Why, and its wording is the owner's.
- **A/B.** The new tests cannot compile against the code before the round, so each was shown to fail by re-editing: 31 mutants in five batches (`mutate.py`; a sixth run repeats one mutant alone), each an exact text edit, the files put back from copies saved before the batch and checked byte-identical. Batch A, the gaps (10 mutants): "✘ Test run with 65 tests in 6 suites failed … with 25 issues", 8 tests: the gap tests above but the smart collection's, which is batch C's, and the late image's. Batch B, the fixes undone (8): 20 issues, 7 tests. - **Green.** The ten figure suites on the fixed build: "✔ Test run with 80 tests in 10 suites passed after 8.462 seconds" (63 before the round: 17 new tests, one of them run once for each storage hub, and one test changed, `anExportFetchesAbsentImages`). Full unit target (`-only-testing FRUSExplorerTests`, iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`, on the final build): **"✔ Test run with 6398 tests in 756 suites passed after 384.652 seconds."**, "** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **"; the test build's only warnings are the two known residues. `CodingStandardsAuditTests` and `EditableContentKeyTests` again with this section in place: "✔ Test run with 80 tests in 2 suites passed after 42.595 seconds.". macOS: `FRUSExplorerMac` "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **" (Xcode 27.0, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`), with no warning beyond the two known residues.
- **Decisions for the owner that this round made or met.**
  - **The pass is automatic.** A full library downloaded before build 49 fetches up to 141 MB of images at its first launch on this build, without being asked, under Allow Cellular Downloads (on unless turned off). That is what D3 says a volume's images are; the alternative is the semantic vectors' — a switch and a button in Volumes & Storage — which needs copy and both hubs.
  - **Nothing on screen says a volume's images are incomplete**, and there is no control to fetch them. The pass tries again at each launch and reconnect.
  - **A quotation taken across a drawn space keeps the glued text.** `.elementSpace` is no flat text, by design, so that no highlight offset moves and nothing re-indexes; a highlight's stored passage and a collection excerpt are cut from flat text, so one taken across any of the 54,025 seams reads "Washington,February 28, 1861" beside a body that now prints the space. Closing it changes flat text and needs a rendering-version bump.
  - **The side-load notice** shown after an import (`settings.hub.sideload.notCatalogued.detail`) names Citation Lookup and Add Documents and does not say a side-loaded volume's figures read "[Figure]". The manuals' proposals say it; the in-app wording is the owner's.
- **Still open after this round.**
  - **The Mac was not run**, by eye or otherwise: a development build shares the owner's store. The reader, the storage hub and the exports are shared code, built for macOS and run on an iPad and an iPhone. Word itself did not open the exported file; its package was checked.
  - **Two images are fetched that no document draws:** the name scan leaves out `<titlePage>` only, so the two figures directly in `<front>` are asked for (`frus1931-41v02` `figure_0007`, 284,620 bytes; `frus1952-54v04` `figure_0001`, refused). A `divDepth > 0` clause in `FigureGraphicScanner` would leave them out and take the fetched total to 552 images, 140,710,237 bytes.
  - **The export header takes no dateline from an `<opener>`** (`renderModelHeadAndDateline` reads top-level nodes only). Pre-existing, met while measuring; not changed.
  - **An image that arrives late still moves the page under a reader who is not at a footnote.** Only a revealed footnote is brought back.

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

The review confirmed ten findings. Two rules reported rows that are not defects, the tests pinned both, and one audit item was missing. All ten are fixed; the report's figures moved in section 6 only.

**What changed in the report's figures.** `transcription.csv` 171 → 169 rows:
- **6.2, 22 notes in 17 volumes → 16 in 14.** The rule was "the note holds `))` and has more `)` than `(`". A note that numbers a list "1) … 2) … 3)" has more `)` than `(` by construction, and any nested "(… (ibid.))" in it supplies the `))`. Six rows were such notes (`frus1950v05` d234fn1, `frus1964-68v13` d44fn4 and d118fn3, `frus1969-76v37` d45fn3, `frus1977-80v12` d306fn2, `frus1981-88v04` d49fn1). The rule now walks the parentheses in order (`_stray_closers`) and sets list enumerators aside; the note must still hold `))`. The row quotes the text up to the `)` that closes nothing: in `frus1961-63v11` d142fn0 that is "…Central Files, 737.56361/11-562)", where round 0 quoted a balanced `))` further on.
- **6.5, 34 datelines in 23 volumes → 30 in 22.** `ohlib.plain()` put a space at every tag, so `D<hi rend="smallcaps">epartment of</hi> S<hi rend="smallcaps">tate</hi>` read "D epartment of S tate" and was matched as a misspelling. Four rows were that (`frus1865p2` d163, `frus1866p1` d25 and d228, `frus1868p1` d159). `plain()` now puts nothing where an inline tag or a footnote stands and a space where any other tag does. The 30 that remain were each read in the run's output; eight with unusual shapes ("Department.of State", "Department of’State", "Department, of State") were opened at their lines and are as quoted.
- **6.1, new: 5 source notes in 2 volumes read "Central Files1967-69" or "Central Files1970-73".** The audit's OH-T4 had two halves and round 0 carried one; the skeptic had confirmed the other at `frus1969-76ve01` lines 41031, 41259, 42364 and 42618. The new rule finds those four and `frus1969-76ve04` line 60065. Part B.3 says so.
- **6.3, "S VIEI": 13 source notes, and now 1 more site** in `frus1961-63v03`'s Sources section (line 6356), which the source-note scan could not see.
- **6.4, doubled full stops 8 → 10.** Not a finding: it follows from the reading above. With no space supplied at a tag, `<hi rend="italic">ibid.</hi>.` (`frus1955-57v21` d69fn1) and `<persName>Feldman, Mark B.</persName>.` (`frus1969-76v22` d127fn1) read "ibid.." and "Mark B..". Both were opened in the file.
- **No quotation holds a space at an inline tag any more.** 28 headings in `missing-documents.csv`, 31 `printed_reference` values and 15 `printed` dates lost the spaces round 0 had put at tags ("( Russell )" → "(Russell)"). No row was added or lost in those files. (This bullet said "Every quotation is now the file's text", and the report said a quotation could be compared with the file character for character. Neither holds where the file has no whitespace at a tag that is not inline: `plain()` still puts a space there, which is 19 of 6.5's 30 datelines at an `<lb/>`. Review fixes, round 2.)

**`--check` (`missing_figures`, `report_to_check`).**

## Session 2026-10-02 — The Subject-Numeric File is its own filing era: an eleventh provenance category, a stored citation form (index v65) and a Source Explorer panel, placed by what the citation gives (lane CFPF; #1543, two fold-ins)

**The question.** #1543: "Subject-Numeric files need to be pulled out of the Central Foreign Policy File and treated as a distinct filing era", in archival analytics and Source Explorer, with NARA's page on the central files' eras as its reference. The lane was added after Tier 3 on the owner's word. Its specification was written first, from seven readers' reports, and the owner answered four questions on it (2026-10-02): the full split; it ships in build 49; the decimal numbers cited through the National Archives move to Central Decimal File; the collection records stay as they are and the help text explains them. Every other decision took the specification's default and is listed in the PR for review.

**What was measured.** Corpus `HistoryAtState/frus` at `8e5da08c1`, 553 manifest volumes. Two note grains: every `type="source"` element (269,242; `source-provenance-index.json`) and one note per document (264,552; `collection-usage-index.json`, Source Explorer, the packet, the live index).
- **The issue's premise does not hold in the data.** Of the 9,443 documents that cite the Subject-Numeric File, 22 were in the Central Foreign Policy File category. 3,844 were in Central Decimal File and 5,577 in Other NARA Collections, by how each note is worded: through the Department (`Department of State, Central Files, POL 27 VIET S` parses as `.centralFiles`), through the National Archives (`National Archives, RG 59, Central Files 1964–66, POL 27 VIET S` parses as `.naraCollection`), or with a remark naming the Central Foreign Policy File (`.cfpfFile`). At the source-element grain: 3,824, 5,468 and 5 of 9,297.
- **The control run.** Before any code change, both generators at the shipped `GENERATED_DATE` (2026-10-01) into scratch: each output byte-identical to the shipped file (`cmp`; SHA-256 `a0e3563a…` and `a57f3920…`).
- **The rule over the corpus**, by a scratch program linking the worktree's `SourceNoteKit` over the specification's two note files. It read every note exactly as the specification's probe did: 0 of 207,600 central-files-shaped parses differ at the source-element grain and 0 of 208,851 at the document grain.

| Category | Source elements, before → after | Documents, before → after |
|---|---|---|
| Central Decimal File | 194,243 → 190,767 | 194,206 → 190,718 (360 → 340 volumes) |
| Subject-Numeric File | 0 → 9,297 (104 volumes) | 0 → 9,443 (112 volumes) |
| Central Foreign Policy File | 3,178 → 3,173 | 4,094 → 4,072 |
| Other NARA Collections | 10,179 → 4,363 | 10,551 → 4,618 |

  The other seven categories and both totals are unmoved. Every figure equals the specification's expected figure; the difference is 0 at both grains.
- **The export generator's measurement run**, into scratch and not committed (the committed `Planning/source-explorer-export/` snapshot is a dated record and is untouched): 264,552 records, `byStrategy` equal to the usage index's categories line for line, every one of the 9,443 Subject-Numeric records with the route `staticSeriesLink` (5,577 parsed as `.naraCollection`, 3,844 as `.centralFiles`, 22 as `.cfpfFile`), and the 356 decimal numbers cited through the National Archives keeping `catalogRecordGroupKeywordQuery`.
- **By what decided it** (documents; source elements in brackets): the class key 7,003 (7,117), a designation the class grammar refuses 2,433 (2,156), the block of years alone 7 (24).
- **By document year:** 1962: 1; 1963: 1,228; 1964: 1,308; 1965: 1,157; 1966: 913; 1967: 1,248; 1968: 985; 1969: 493; 1970: 536; 1971: 730; 1972: 586; 1973: 258; none later, and none with no date.

**What changed.**
- **The rule** (`SourceNoteKit/CollectionKeying.swift`, 1.6). `centralFilesReading(parsed:note:)` reads the form of an RG 59 central-files citation — `.decimal` or `.subjectNumeric` — with what decided it and the file designation. It never reads the document's year. `ParsedSourceNote` gains no case, so no collection identity moves.
  - Gate: `.centralFiles` in RG 59; `.naraCollection` in RG 59 with no lot, an anchor (a segment that leads with the central files' name, `Decimal File`, or `CF`) and a clean lead (every segment before the anchor is a holder or record-group phrase); `.cfpfFile` with an anchor, a clean lead and no lot or film form in its citation sentence, which answers `.subjectNumeric` or nothing.
  - Evidence, first that applies: the class key (letter-led is Subject-Numeric, digit-led decimal); a stored identifier or a segment after the anchor that opens with a handbook category or one of seven organization leads (`AID`, `UN`, `NATO`, `SEATO`, `CENTO`, `EEC`, `OECD`), in capitals or in title case of three or four letters; a block of years with both ends in 1964–1973, unless a later segment opens with `Entry`, `Records of` or `Lot`.
  - Readers: `centralFilesForm`, `isSubjectNumericCitation`, `centralFileDesignation`, `subjectNumericLead(ofCandidate:)`, `printedSubjectNumericBlock(inCitation:)`.
- **Generators.** `ProvenanceCategory.subjectNumericFile`, second of eleven; `from(_:note:)` replaces the one-argument form at its three call sites. `ExportClassification.liveLookupRoute(for:note:)` records the static link for a Subject-Numeric citation. `source-provenance-index.json` and `collection-usage-index.json` regenerated at `GENERATED_DATE=2026-10-02`: in the first only the category counts move (269,242 notes, 523 volumes, 16 decades as before); in the second only `categories`, `volumeCategories` and `generated`. No other artifact is touched (`git diff --stat` over `FRUSExplorer/Resources` names those two files).
- **Live index, v64 → v65** (`IndexingPipeline` 4.27). `citation_era` gains `subject_numeric`; a decimal number worded through the National Archives is stored `decimal`. 9,799 rows change form (9,443 and 356). Repository, record group, `series_name` and `decimal_class` are written as before. `relatedByDecimal` reads both forms; `archivalLibraryCollectionGroups` is unchanged, so Your Library stops listing "Central Files 1970–73" as a collection.
- **App category.** `SourceProvenanceCategory.subjectNumericFile`, "Subject-Numeric File", second; `from(citationEra:repository:)` maps `subject_numeric`.
- **Source Explorer, both twins.** `SourceExplorerView.subjectNumericCitation(parsed:note:documentDay:)` and a panel in every wording: the type "State Dept. Subject-Numeric File (February 1963–1973)", RG 59, the file designation, the block of years (the note's when it prints one of NARA's three, else the document's date: February–December 1963, 1964–66, 1967–69, 1970–73), what to hand an archivist, NARA's page and the handbook for the block (both when the block is unknown). No keyed catalog search runs for these notes (`CatalogQueryEvidence.forNote(_:rawNote:)`, and a return before each view's query switch). The Archival Neighbors basis line is the iOS view's alone — the Mac view draws none, as on `v2` — and it reads "Same Subject-Numeric file — POL 27 VIET S" for a citation worded through the National Archives. A Department-led designation has no line, with or without a stop in it (review round 1, below). The no-year table gains "1973–1979 (Central Foreign Policy File)" and its 1963–1973 row reads "February 1963–1973 (Subject-Numeric File)"; the NARA Lookup sheet draws the same table.
- **Archives Visit packet.** No stored key moves. A central-file row whose repository is the National Archives keeps `coll|National Archives|<series>`; the model reads a `coll|` key under a central category as a collection-form target; a roster row with no parsed designation takes the rule's; a Subject-Numeric target is a central-file target (no-box line, College Park, NARA's Example 7 by category or by the designation's form).

**Where the code departs from the specification, and why.**
- **Three more functions than the five it lists.** `centralFilesReading` returns the evidence and the lead beside the form, because the audit above needs them from the real code and not from a second implementation; `subjectNumericLead(ofCandidate:)` and `printedSubjectNumericBlock(inCitation:)` are public so their rules have tests of their own.
- **One of its fixtures contradicts its own rule.** It lists `…Central Files 1970–73, Inter-American Affairs.` as giving no form, to show that a five-letter title-case lead is refused. The lead is refused, and the block then decides: by rule 3 the note is Subject-Numeric, as a folder title under a 1970–73 block is. The tests pin both halves: the same note with no block gives no form, and with the block it is `.subjectNumeric` by `.block`.
- **The basis line follows the route.** The specification gives the new line to every citation worded through the National Archives that has a class key. 192 National-Archives-led Subject-Numeric notes (179 in `frus1964-68v34`, which prints "RG 59, Records of the Department of State, Central Files, 1964–66, …"), 173 of them with a class key, store a series that does not name the central files, so their neighbours come from the collection route. They keep the collection line. The new line is given only where the route is the class route.
- **The Mac's manual search field.** A Subject-Numeric citation worded through the National Archives is a `.naraCollection`, which the Mac view offered its free-text search field. Its box now shows the finding aids, so a search there would show nothing; the field is withheld (`CatalogQueryEvidence.offersManualSearch`, in the shared type so it has a test).
- **Smaller.** The probe also carried `OAS` as an organization lead and accepted title case of any length; the specification's seven leads and three-or-four letters are used, and no corpus note is read differently. The probe dropped a leading `RG 59` only before "Cen"; the code drops it before any anchor words, with the same result. `targetKey`'s `where` is written on each pattern, since in a multi-pattern case it binds only the pattern it follows.
- **Comments the specification did not list** that counted ten categories or carried the map's old figure are corrected (`TopCollectionsCard.swift`, `ArchivesBrowseView.swift`, `SemanticMapExport.swift`). That pass missed eight, which review round 1 corrected: `ArchivesBrowseView.swift:19`, `TopCollectionsCard.swift:17`, `SourceProvenanceDashboard.swift:557`, two in `SemanticMapSpikeView.swift` (`:1231`, `:3175`), `CollectionUsageIndexRunner.swift:182`, a test comment (`ArchivalLibraryQueryTests.swift:310`), and `IndexingPipeline.archivalLibraryGroups`' "eight citation forms", which are nine.

The release paragraph's by-eye checks gain the lane's seven, and "HYG, READ and CFPF built the Mac app without running it".

*Smaller findings left, and why.*
- **A basis line on the Mac.** `MacSourceExplorerView` draws none, on `v2` as here. It is twin drift older than the lane, already in the PR's list.
- **The panel's block for a date coarser than a day.** `subjectNumericCitation` takes the document's day, and `DocumentDay` is nil at month or year grain, so a note that prints no block then shows no File Years row and both handbooks. The decimal panel it replaced fell back to the document's year. Of the 3,911 Subject-Numeric documents that print none of NARA's three blocks (3,837 with no range, 70 "1960–63" and 4 "1964–67"; a regex over the same notes found 3,910 of them), 8 have corpus date bounds more than a day apart, 6 of them inside one year of 1964–1973. That is the ceiling, since the index may store a range at day grain. Left because the fix changes the reader's signature at three call sites in both views for at most 8 documents: pass `effectiveYear` and take the block from it when there is no day and the year is 1964–1973 (1963 alone cannot say, January being before the file).

### Landing (2026-10-02)

`origin/v2` was still `6ab2afc1`, the commit the lane was developed on, so there was no merge. The landing made one code change and two corrections, and ran the gates on the result.

**The Archival Neighbors empty state under the Subject-Numeric panel** (round 1 left it as owner copy; the session's orchestrator decided it is fixed here, with wording the owner can edit in review, because the screen contradicted itself). Both views printed "This source note doesn’t cite a recognized lot file, central file, or presidential library, so related documents can’t be matched" (`source.explorer.related.empty.unmatched`) under the panel that names the note's central file, whenever `supportsArchivalNeighbors` was false and the list was empty.

*When a Subject-Numeric citation gets no neighbours*, read from `IndexingPipeline.relatedDocuments`, `archivalNeighborsWithCohort`, `relatedByDecimal`, `relatedByDecimalClass` and `ParsedSourceNote.archivalNeighborKey`, and counted over the 264,552 document notes by a scratch program linking the worktree's `SourceNoteKit` (9,443 Subject-Numeric documents):
- **3,842 have a parse-level key** and already read "No other indexed documents cite this archival source" when the list is empty: 3,657 Department-led notes whose designation the parse stored (`relatedByDecimal`, on the stored file number), 182 National-Archives-led notes whose series does not name the central files (`relatedByCollection`), and 3 whose remark carries a film number. Unchanged.
- **4,083 have no parse-level key and are matched all the same**: worded through the National Archives, the stored series names the central files, and `SourceNoteParser.decimalClassLocation(inCitation:)` reads a class key, which `relatedByDecimalClass` matches against the stored `decimal_class`. `archivalNeighborKey` is nil for them by design, so an empty list read as "unmatched". 399 of them cite a class no other document in the corpus stores; the rest are empty only while the volumes that share the class are not indexed.
- **1,518 have nothing to match on**, and no arm of `relatedDocuments` serves them: 1,302 worded the same way with no class key (902 designations with no subject number, `POL FR-US`; 393 with one that the class grammar still refuses, `ORG 4–COMM`, `SP 1–1 US– USSR`; 7 that give only their block), 184 Department-led with no stored identifier (`AID (US) S VIET`), 3 Department-led with an identifier the file-number route cannot read (`POL/7 US/ Harriman`), 19 parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File, and 10 National-Archives-led notes whose parse kept no series (`RG 59 Central Files 1967–69, …`, no comma after the record group). Round 1's "about 1,500" is this figure. The collection authority's alias fallback can still fill a list for some of them, by collection name and not by file; that needs a live index and was not measured. (It no longer can: round 2, below.)
- **"A designation with no subject number cannot be matched" is not what the code does**, so no sentence says it: a Department-led `POL US–USSR` is stored and matched whole, and 393 designations that have a number are not matched.

*The fix.* `SourceExplorerView.relatedEmptyState(for:note:)` is the rule both views ask, static so a test drives it: a key gives `.noNeighbors`; a Subject-Numeric citation (`CollectionKeying.isSubjectNumericCitation`) with no key gives `.subjectNumericNoNeighbors` when the class route has a key and `.subjectNumericUnkeyed` when nothing does; any other note gives `.unmatched`. Each view's `relatedEmptyMessage` prints one sentence per state, the same key and text in both:
- `source.explorer.related.empty.subjectNumeric`: "This source note cites the Subject-Numeric File. No other indexed document was matched to the same file. Index more volumes to surface related documents."
- `source.explorer.related.empty.subjectNumeric.unkeyed`: "This source note cites the Subject-Numeric File, but not in a form the app can match on, so documents from the same file can’t be matched."

Two keys and not one, because only the first state changes when more volumes are indexed. The other two sentences are unchanged. EditableContent: two blocks added beside the unmatched one in `06-Archives.md` (267 blocks), 38 ranged blocks re-pointed, one Amendment-Log bullet. `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md`: one entry in the lane's section, for both manuals' Archival Neighbors paragraph, which says an empty list always means no other document cites the source.

*How it was verified.* iPhone 17, iOS 26.5 (`A36F4C02`), Xcode 27.0; every A/B by re-editing the file and writing the saved text back, never `git checkout`; `-only-testing FRUSExplorerTests/SubjectNumericExplorerTests` on both sides.
- **A/B.** With the rule answering as the screen did (a key gives `.noNeighbors`, anything else `.unmatched`) and both views' `relatedEmptyMessage` as on `c79ff1f4`: "✘ Test run with 16 tests in 1 suite failed after 0.107 seconds with 9 issues." — `emptyNeighbourStates` on each of its seven fixtures, and `bothTwinsSayWhyTheListIsEmpty` once per view. With the fix: "✔ Test run with 16 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.086 seconds." `otherEmptyStatesAreUnmoved` and the scan's own test, `emptySentenceScanReadsEachArm`, pass on both sides, by construction.
- **Eight mutants, one at a time**, each failing the test named for it: the series conjunct dropped (the note with no series, 1 issue); the class-key conjunct dropped (the three notes with no class key, 3); any parse with a class key (the no-series note and the Central Foreign Policy File note, 2); the Subject-Numeric guard dropped (`otherEmptyStatesAreUnmoved`, 2); the key test moved after the Subject-Numeric test (`otherEmptyStatesAreUnmoved`, 3); the two states traded (7); and two scan-only mutants with no rebuild, the Mac view handing the rule another note (1) and the iOS view printing the unmatched sentence for an unkeyed file (3).
- **Not looked at on a screen:** either new sentence. The by-eye list above has them in its Source Explorer item, and the plan of record's release list in its first.

### Landing, round 2 (2026-10-02)

Before the push the lane's build was looked at on an iPhone (iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`; five real volumes indexed by the app itself — `frus1961-63v03`, `frus1961-63v25`, `frus1964-68v01`, `frus1969-76v30`, `frus1969-76ve09p2`, 1,784 documents). It found five defects. This round fixes three, leaves two with their reasons, and corrects three slips in the documents. `origin/v2` was still `6ab2afc1`, so there was again no merge.

**What the pass saw and found right.** The Subject-Numeric panel on seven documents (Type, Record Group, File Designation, File Years — "1963" for `frus1961-63v25/d61`, whose note prints "1960–63" — the request note, the period row, one handbook link and the hint), with no catalog spinner and no key prompt on any. The decimal and Central Foreign Policy File panels, unchanged. The eleven-row period table in the NARA Lookup sheet. Eleven Provenance Types doors whose counts sum to the header's 264,552. The dashboard's legend, Categories menu ("Categories: 10 shown" after one is hidden), "eleven broad categories" and the caveat. The map's provenance legend and its caption ("86 of the 499 volumes"). Your Library's caption, whose 614 central-file notes are the index's 102 decimal, 434 Subject-Numeric and 78 Central Foreign Policy File rows. Both new empty-state sentences, each on a document that should have it.

**The five defects.**
1. **Archival Neighbors listed unrelated documents for a central-file document alone in its file.** `frus1964-68v01/d359` (`POL 13 VIET S`, the only document with that designation in the index) showed a count of 6: two decimal documents of `frus1961-63v25` and four 1973 documents of `frus1969-76ve09p2`. `frus1961-63v03/d10` (`751K.5/1-1163`) showed the same six under "Same decimal file — 751K.5, 1960–January 1963". So the landing's claim that a Department-led designation with no neighbour reads "No other indexed documents cite this archival source" was untrue on screen. Fixed.
2. **With a status banner showing, the eleventh Provenance Types door rests under it** and is visible only while a drag is held. Left: it is every list's last row, not this list's. See "Left".
3. **The provenance charts drew two categories alike that were not alike before.** Central Decimal File and Named File Series (6,343 notes) were the same blue; on `v2` the decimal file's twin was Foreign Archives (74 notes). Every category after the first had changed colour against `v2`. Fixed.
4. **Your Library's composition bar was a line one or two pixels high** at iPhone width. Fixed.
5. **`frus1969-76ve09p2/d84`'s footer reads "Matching archival source: CFPF film D760430"**, a film number from the note's remark. Left: it is the parser's whole-note Central Foreign Policy File test, already in the lane's out-of-scope list (426 notes).

**The charts' colours (3).** The four charts that colour by provenance category — Archival Sourcing's trend and composition, Your Library's composition and bands — gave Swift Charts a domain and no range, so each category took the default cycle's colour for its position. The cycle has seven colours, and the eleventh category sits second, so every later category moved one along. `SourceProvenanceCategory.chartColor` now states each colour and `View.provenanceCategoryColorScale()` applies the scale (`FRUSExplorer/SeriesAnalytics/SourceProvenanceDashboard.swift`, the one place); the four charts call it and state no scale of their own.
- **The ten older categories keep the colour `v2` drew them in**, by their position among the ten: Central Decimal File blue, Central Foreign Policy File green, Lot Files orange, Presidential Libraries purple, Other NARA Collections red, Intelligence Records teal, Named File Series yellow, Foreign Archives blue, Previously Published green, Other / Unclassified orange. The Subject-Numeric File is **brown**, which the cycle never uses. Brown and not indigo, pink or mint, which sit beside the cycle's blue and purple, its red, and its teal. The legend's order is still the enum's, the Subject-Numeric File second.
- **The cycle was measured, not taken from a document.** A chart with a domain and no range was drawn beside the named system colours and its pixels read (macOS 27.0, light and dark): blue, green, orange, purple, red, **teal**, yellow. The sixth is `Color.teal` (0, 195, 208), not `.cyan` (0, 192, 232). The first pass's screenshot of the iOS 26.4 simulator reads the same seven, and a `simctl` screenshot of this round's build reads those values back for the ten categories in `v2`'s order, with (172, 127, 94) for the new one.
- **This reverses the cost the specification's owner decision 3 accepted** ("every later category's colour shifts by one"). No older category changes colour, so a picture of these charts taken before the lane is out of date only by the new band.
- **Not changed:** the ten already had three pairs drawn alike (the decimal file and Foreign Archives, the Central Foreign Policy File and Previously Published, Lot Files and Other / Unclassified), and still have. Eleven colours of their own would recolour every one of these charts and is the owner's to decide. The map's provenance lens has its own palette and is untouched.

**Your Library's composition bar (4).** The chart had a fixed height of 120 points, legend included (`ArchivalAnalyticsView.libraryCompositionCard`). At an iPhone's width the eleven legend entries wrap to six rows and take all of it. The floor is now on the plot: the plot area has a minimum and ideal height of 40 points and may grow, and the chart a minimum height of 120 (`ArchivalAnalyticsView.libraryCompositionChart(_:)`, static so a test draws it).
- **Measured.** Drawn 345 points wide on the iOS 26.5 simulator with a note in every category: before, "the bar is 1 points high in a chart of 120"; after, the chart is taller than 120 and the bar at least 20. On screen (iPhone 17, 402 points wide, five volumes) the bar is 28 points high. Drawn 1,000 points wide it is 120 high on both sides.
- **The Mac and a wide iPad.** A scratch program drew the same chart on macOS 27.0 at six widths with the old and the new modifiers. At 1,000 points both are 120 high with a 43-point bar. At 600 and 700 points the old chart's plot was already about 40, and the new chart is 121 high: one point. Below that the old chart's bar is 12 points at 500 wide and nothing at 345, and the new chart grows (143 and 187 high). So the cards are unmoved where the legend fits in two or three rows, and a narrow window or a large text size gets the fix too.
- **Not changed:** the bands chart below it (260 points; its plot is about 75 on an iPhone, read off this round's screenshot) and the dashboard's two charts (300 points; about 115) have room under an eleven-entry legend.

**Archival Neighbors for a central-file document (1).** The cause, reproduced in a unit test through the real writer and query before anything was changed:
- When the direct route finds nothing, `archivalNeighborsWithCohort` resolves the note to a collection-authority record and matches the record's names against `series_name` (`aliasNeighbors`). A Department-led central-files citation with a class key resolves to the record "Central Files" (`txt:department of state|central file`, cited by 157 volumes), which the app's own help calls a filing system rather than a collection. `directKeys` gives a `.centralFiles` parse no record group, so the match is `relatedBySeriesName("Central Files")`: every row whose stored series is that name or begins with it and a comma, with no test of the file or the form. (The by-eye pass read the cause as `relatedByCollection(RG 59, "Central Files")`; that is the same match with a record-group clause, and it is the path of a National-Archives-led anchor, where the record's first name is skipped as the anchor's own series.)
- The rows it matches are the notes worded with a comma after the name: `National Archives, RG 59, Central Files, 1970–73, POL 23 Oman` parses with the series `Central Files`. On the unfixed code the test's anchor listed all five such documents with the basis "Central Files (collection authority)" and a cohort of 6.
- **The fix** is one rule at the one place the anchored path runs the fallback: `IndexingPipeline.aliasFallbackServes(_:note:)` refuses it for a `.centralFiles` parse and for any note `CollectionKeying.centralFilesReading` reads (a National-Archives-led RG 59 note; a note parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File that gives a Subject-Numeric designation). Every other note keeps the fallback as on `v2`: a lot file, a library collection, a named series, a record-group series, and a library-led note the parser read as the Central Foreign Policy File from its remark. Nothing stored changes, so there is no index version.
- **Every caller.** The fallback for a document runs only in `archivalNeighborsWithCohort`. `archivalNeighbors(forVolumeId:documentId:)` is a wrapper on it, and its callers are Source Explorer's inline list on iOS and on the Mac, the Archival Neighbors sheet and window for a document (`ArchivalNeighborsRequest.document`, `ArchivalNeighborsSheet.init(appState:docKey:)`), and Related Documents' archival generator (`SimilarityGenerators`, which calls the cohort form). So the count in the list's header, the list, the cohort chip and the Mac twin agree. `relatedDocuments(for:)`, the unanchored path, never ran the fallback. `archivalNeighborCounts(forKeys:)` leaves it out by its own documented decision and badges front-matter rows, not documents.
- **Measured** over the corpus's 264,552 document notes, by a scratch program linking the worktree's `SourceNoteKit` and reading the bundled authority (not a full index): 17,543 Department-led documents resolve to the "Central Files" record, and at least 998 of them are alone in their file (no other document stores the number before the slash; the route's year segments can only add to that). 71 documents in 23 volumes store a series that record's name matches, so on a full index each of those 998 would have listed 30 of the 71. Another 11 Department-led documents and 6 parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File resolve to a block's record (`Central Files 1967–69`, `1970–73`), whose name matches the National-Archives-led documents that spell the block that way (1,779 and 1,973 notes resolve to those two records). The rule refuses the fallback for 200,161 notes in all (194,206 `.centralFiles`, 5,933 National-Archives-led, 22 parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File).
- **The empty states are unmoved.** `relatedEmptyState(for:note:)` does not read the list, so no condition changed and `SubjectNumericExplorerTests` is as it was. What changed is that the sentences are now what a reader sees: `frus1964-68v01/d359` and `frus1961-63v03/d10` read "No other indexed documents cite this archival source. Index more volumes to surface related documents." with no count and no basis line, and no Subject-Numeric citation's list is filled from the authority. The landing left that unmeasured for the 1,518 documents with nothing to match on; it is now zero by the rule.
- **Not changed, and worth a look:** a volume's own Sources row "Central Files" still lists by that name (`archivalNeighbors(forLotFile:…)`, the front-matter path, where the row IS the filing system); and a National-Archives-led note whose stored series is `Records of the Department of State` still takes the direct series route (the 182 of the landing's count).

**Left.**
- **The status banner over a list's last row (2).** Not local to Provenance Types, so not changed here. `MainTabView` applies the indexing and iCloud banner as a bottom `safeAreaInset` on each tab's root (`FRUSExplorer/App/MainTabView.swift:175`, `:199`, `:207`, `:215`; Search's at `:184`), from outside the root's own `NavigationStack`, and a stack does not pass that inset to its content. The file says so itself at `:651–656` (`tabShellBottomOverlay`: "the banner is drawn over the content rather than beside it"), and only the Search tab publishes the banner's height, which only `SearchView`'s pre-search screen reads. `ArchivesBrowseView` has no bottom margin, and neither has any other Browse list. Seen again this round on the Settings tab (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, signed out of iCloud): at rest the list ends on the "Diagnostics" heading and its one row is under the banner. **Proposed, as its own issue:** publish the measured height on all five tabs and reserve it once inside each tab's stack (`.contentMargins(.bottom, height, for: .scrollContent)` on the stack's content), or move the banner inside each stack as #486 did for the top banner; with a UI test that scrolls a list to its end under the Local Only banner (`FRUS_UI_TEST_MODE` shows it) and requires the last row's frame above the banner's. It touches every tab and the keyboard rule of #1070, which is why it is not a rider here.
- **The film number in `frus1969-76ve09p2/d84`'s footer (5).** The parser's whole-note test, out of scope as before.
- **Seen by the pass and not acted on**, none of them made by this lane's code except the first, which is owner decision 9: "Which collections carried this scope" still ranks the three block records as collections; three figures print without a thousands separator ("Showing 12 of 1833 collections", "carrying 17613 here against 7069", "the 1669 source notes"); the NARA Lookup sheet's title is cut short on its first paint, and the data-table sheet's ("Archival provenance over ti…"); the two handbook links of the period table's Subject-Numeric row sit 16 points apart; the map kept the Regions colours for about three seconds under the Provenance legend; a Department-led file's neighbours cross NARA's blocks of years (`frus1964-68v01/d5`: 107 rows, one of them in the 1963 volume) under a File Years of "1964–66"; and a document with nothing to match on has siblings on the device that the app cannot list (eleven other `frus1961-63v03` documents cite `AID (US) S VIET`).

**The trend chart's holes.** Series analytics ▸ Archival Sourcing ▸ "Archival provenance over time" is a stacked area chart of each category's share of a decade's source notes.
- **The cause, confirmed in the code and by drawing the chart.** `SourceProvenanceData`'s share rows held a row only for a category with notes in the decade: the bundled `byDecade` counts omit zeros, and the unfiltered path skipped a zero count. The filtered path, which the second pass expected to be whole, skipped it too: it kept zero rows only for a decade the filter leaves with no shown notes at all (Session 3's review). Swift Charts draws a band between its own points and stacks the bands above it on what is present at each decade. So a band with no point in the decade before its first notes begins as a vertical edge, and the bands above it, already stacked on it at that decade and not at the one before, leave a white wedge between. The Subject-Numeric File has notes in the 1960s (6,842 of 24,456, 28%) and the 1970s only.
- **Measured.** The second pass's screenshot of round 2's build (`eye2/L27-sourcing-chart1.png`, 3 pixels a point): 238 of the stack's 583 pixel columns hold a background pixel between their first and last chart colour, the worst 92 of the plot's 342 rows (27%), just before 1960. The `v2` screenshot (`eye-v2/22-sourcing-chart1.png`): 173 of 583, the worst 36 of 406 rows (9%), under the Central Foreign Policy File's start. Both have more columns with a hole than the three wedges the pass named, because every category that is absent from a decade between two it has notes in leaves a sliver (Other NARA Collections has notes in the 1910s and the 1940s and none between).
- **The fix.** The share rows are dense: every shown category has a row in every decade, with a share of zero where it has no notes, on both paths (`SourceProvenanceData.init` and `shareByDecade(in:excluding:)`, `FRUSExplorer/SeriesAnalytics/SourceProvenanceData.swift`). A band now runs from zero and to zero, and the stack is closed. The chart itself is `SourceProvenanceDashboard.provenanceMixChart(_:domain:)`, static so a test draws the card's own chart. Over the bundled index the rows are 99 (nine decades of eleven categories) where they were 65.

Over the bundled index that is the 65 lines the table had, each with the share it had, and no "Subject-Numeric File, 1950, 0.0%". Under the category filter a decade with no shown notes keeps its 0.0% lines, as before. - **The rule now.** A Subject-Numeric citation whose key IS its file — a `.centralFiles` parse with a key — is `.subjectNumericNoNeighbors`, as the class route is. Each shape, with the sentence it prints when its list is empty:

  - *Parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File, with a film number from a remark* (`frus1969-76ve09p2/d84`): matched on the film. The generic sentence, as before.
  - *Nothing to match on* (`POL FR-US` through the National Archives, `AID (US) S VIET` through the Department, a block alone): "…not in a form the app can match on…", as before.
  - *Not a Subject-Numeric citation:* its own two sentences, as before.

## Session 2026-10-02 — The CloudKit schema gate's first read: fifteen fields Production never held, deployed in the twelfth promotion

The owner saved a CloudKit management token and ran `./Scripts/check_cloudkit_schema.py` for build 49. It failed.
- **The finding.** Fifteen identifiers the inventory attested as deployed were absent from Production: `CD_ArchiveVisitDocument.CD_stateData`, `CD_ArchiveVisitPlan.CD_deliverableTogglesData` and `.CD_inquiryText`, `CD_ArchiveVisitTarget.CD_stateData` and `.CD_userNote`, `CD_Collection.CD_introductionRichText`, `.CD_introductionText` and `.CD_subtitle`, `CD_CollectionEntry.CD_includeFootnotesOverride`, `.CD_includeRelatedDocuments`, `.CD_includeSourceNoteOverride` and `.CD_summaryPromptIdOverride`, `CD_DocumentHighlight.CD_noteId`, and `CD_SavedSearch.CD_dateRangeEnd` and `.CD_dateRangeStart`.
  - The first ten were in the inventory since it began (2026-07-26), the five Archive Visit fields since the eighth promotion (2026-08-26).
  - The raw `cktool export-schema` files for Production and Development were byte-identical (27,003 bytes) and held none of them. That is what a Development environment reset to Production looks like, so no deploy could have carried them.
  - A record saved with one of them set on a TestFlight build since then would have failed to upload (#1531's shape). Not measured on any device.
- **The fix.** The Development export plus the fifteen fields, each typed as the mirror types its analogues (`String`/`UUID` STRING QUERYABLE SEARCHABLE SORTABLE, `Data` BYTES QUERYABLE SORTABLE, `Bool` INT64 QUERYABLE SORTABLE, `Date` TIMESTAMP QUERYABLE SORTABLE; all fifteen are optional with no external storage).
  - `cktool validate-schema` passed, and the owner ran `cktool import-schema` into Development.
  - The gate read against Development then passed. The owner deployed to Production, and the gate's read against Production passed: 268 required identifiers held, 310 in all. It wrote the stamp the archive phase reads in the main checkout.
- **The record.** `CloudKitSchemaInventory` 2.0 records the twelfth promotion; `deployedThroughBuild` 48 → 49 and `deployedOn` → 2026-10-02. The baseline count and digest do not move.
- **Not done:** no device check that the records which failed before now upload.

## Session 2026-10-04 — TEIHeaderKit, SemanticVectorsKit and FTS5Store compile on Linux behind `canImport` guards, and Apple platforms compile what they did before

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`), the self-hosted web edition, compiles this repository's kits on Linux from a pinned submodule. Today it compiles SourceNoteKit, CrossRefKit, GeneratorKit and four pure-Swift files of FTS5Store. It is meant to compile these three kits as well, and they did not build on Linux. The owner lifted the hold on that project's pull requests here on 2026-10-04, and this is its first. Branched from `v2` @ `34a51205`. Guards only, and one named Linux skip: nothing changes on an Apple platform.

**What failed on Linux** (`swift:6.4-noble`, arm64, at `34a51205`)
- TEIHeaderKit: "'XMLParser' is unavailable: This type has moved to the FoundationXML module. Import that module to use it." (`TEIHeaderParser.swift:162`, `:209`, `:214`, `:292`), and "cannot find type 'XMLParserDelegate' in scope" (`:98`).
- SemanticVectorsKit: "no such module 'CryptoKit'" (`SemanticVectorsArtifacts.swift:15`).
- FTS5Store: "no such module 'SQLite3'" (`FTS5Connection.swift:10`); with that file guarded, "no such module 'OSLog'" (`FTS5Store.swift:10`). Seven FTS5StoreTests files import SQLite3.
- ManifestGeneratorCore, whose test target also holds TEIHeaderKit's tests (`TEIHeaderParserTests.swift`): "'URLSession' is unavailable: This type has moved to the FoundationNetworking module. Import that module to use it." (`GitHubClient.swift:44`, `TEIHeaderFetcher.swift:49`). swift-corelibs-foundation has no `URLSession.bytes(for:)` either.

**Changed**
- **Imports.** Each is inside `#if canImport`, and on an Apple platform each guard selects the import that was there before: SQLite3, else `CSQLite` (`FTS5Connection`, `FTS5Store`, `FTS5Vocabulary` and the seven test files); OSLog (`FTS5Store`); CryptoKit, else swift-crypto's `Crypto` (`SemanticVectorsArtifacts`). `FoundationXML` (`TEIHeaderParser`) and `FoundationNetworking` (`GitHubClient`, `TEIHeaderFetcher`) are imported only where they exist, which is not on an Apple platform, since Apple's Foundation holds those types itself.
- **`TEIHeaderFetcher.fetch`.** Its guard tests the Linux module first. Under `#if canImport(FoundationNetworking)` it reads the response whole with `data(for:)` and replays its bytes into the unchanged `</teiHeader>` scan. Apple platforms take the `#else`, which still streams with `bytes(for:)`.
- **`FTS5Store/LinuxLogger.swift`, new:** an `os.Logger` stand-in with the same call shape, `privacy:` interpolation included, that writes `[level] category: message` to standard error. All of it is inside `#if !canImport(OSLog)`. `xcodegen generate` put it in both app targets, the 6 lines of `project.pbxproj` it added and nothing else; the schemes were restored.
- **One named Linux skip.** FTS5StoreTests' "Database file has isExcludedFromBackupKey set after creation" is `.enabled(if: platformKeepsBackupExclusion, …)`. The constant is true under `canImport(Darwin)`. The trait itself sits outside any guard, and on Apple platforms it is true, so the test runs there as before. On Linux it skips with its reason, "Linux: swift-corelibs-foundation keeps no backup attribute, so excluding a file from backup is a silent no-op". Measured in the container: `setResourceValue(true, forKey: .isExcludedFromBackupKey)` throws nothing, and reading the key back gives nil.
- Version-history entries in the eleven touched files that carry a block. `Package.swift` is unchanged. FRUS Explorer Light is to declare `Crypto` and `CSQLite`, for Linux only, in its own package, in the pull request there that moves its pin.

**Apple platforms: nothing changes, and how that was checked**
- **`canImport` on Xcode 27.0's SDKs** (Swift 6.4), by `swiftc -typecheck` of a probe file for macOS, the iOS Simulator and iOS: SQLite3, OSLog, CryptoKit and Darwin are true; FoundationXML, FoundationNetworking, CSQLite and Crypto are false. So on an Apple platform each guard selects the code that was there before: the `SQLite3`, `OSLog` and `CryptoKit` imports; `TEIHeaderFetcher`'s `#else`, with `bytes(for:)`; no `FoundationXML` or `FoundationNetworking` import; and nothing from `LinuxLogger.swift`.
- **`FRUSExplorerMac`**, clean, unsigned Debug, beside `v2` @ `34a51205` built the same way: "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **" both (41 s and 39 s), with identical warning lines, the two known residues only. Each build's `FRUS Explorer.debug.dylib` defines the same 238,006 symbols. The touched files' object files define the same symbols on both (`FTS5Store.o` 834, `FTS5Connection.o` 189, `FTS5Vocabulary.o` 164, `TEIHeaderParser.o` 366, `SemanticVectorsArtifacts.o` 812). `LinuxLogger.o` defines nothing of its own, only the force-load and reflection-version symbols every object in the module carries.
- **iOS 27.0**, a new iPhone 17 simulator (`ACF59CFF`): a clean `build-for-testing` of `FRUSExplorer`, "** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **" in 130 s, with the two known residues only. The full unit target (`test-without-building -collect-test-diagnostics never -only-testing FRUSExplorerTests`, `TEST_RUNNER_FRUS_TEI_MIRROR` set, the app removed first): **"✔ Test run with 6470 tests in 760 suites passed after 400.340 seconds."**, "** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **". `v2`, the same way: "✔ Test run with 6470 tests in 760 suites passed after 350.690 seconds." None is mirror-gated; the mirror-gated suites ran, "External citations — generator/app parity (#784)" among them.

It was `FigureReaderTests`' "A late image does not bring the reader back to a footnote they have since scrolled away from" (`FRUSOffsetEngineTests.swift:2024`): "the page was scrolled back to a note the reader had left: FootnotePlace(scrollY: 3612.0, …)". ## Session 2026-10-04 — FRUSCoreKit, part 1: the TEI parser, the AST, the render conversion, the HTML serializer and the citation code are a Foundation-only kit of their own that builds on Linux, and the app compiles the same files

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`), the self-hosted web edition, compiles this repository's kits on Linux from a pinned submodule; #1567 made the six it needed so far build there. Its reader and its Cite need the TEI pipeline and the citation code, which lived in `FRUSExplorer/` beside the views, where no package target could name them. This is part 1 of `FRUSCoreKit`, the library that project's specification asks for. Part 2, the indexer and search, is later work, and so are the citation matcher, the block splitter and `PageRangeStore`, which need them. Branched from `v2` @ `cfc0d3c6`. There is no re-index, no index-version bump, no CloudKit schema change and no new dependency.

**Changed**
- **`FRUSCoreKit/`, beside `FRUSExplorer/`**, with subfolders that mirror the app's. Thirteen files moved there by `git mv` with no line changed (the first commit is renames only): the parser, the AST, the render nodes, the converter and the HTML serializer (`TEI/`); the citation formatter, models, parser, canonical URL and page-span resolver (`Citation/`); `BrokenRefsIndex` (`CrossReference/`); `VolumeStructure` (`Browser/`); `ManifestModels` (`Models/Manifest/`). Their ten suites moved to `FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/`. `project.yml` compiles `FRUSCoreKit` in both app targets, like `TEIHeaderKit`; `xcodegen` regenerated the project at each commit that added a file, and the schemes were restored.
- **The kit names nothing outside itself.** What it used from Apple-only files moved in, verbatim, and the app keeps each old name as a forwarder or typealias: `FRUSURLScheme` (`CrossRefDestination`, `resolveCrossRefTarget`, `figureHost`, `figureURL(for:)`, `isSafeComponent`; `FRUSURLSchemeHandler` and `FigureImageLibrary` forward), `HighlightColor` (`DocumentHighlight.Color` is a typealias) and `ExportHighlight`, and `FRUSASTNode+PrintedText.swift` (the printed-text walk and `normalizedWhitespace` from `IndexingPipeline.swift`, and `StoredSourceNote.normalizeWrapper`, which `normalizeSourceNoteWrapper` forwards to). Each Apple-only half of a kit type moved out to a file of its own in the app, unchanged: `DocumentJump+NavigationPath.swift`, `CitationStyle+Preference.swift`, `BrokenRefsIndexStore.swift`.
- **Linux guards**, each selecting the old code on an Apple platform: `CryptoKit`, else swift-crypto's `Crypto` (the converter); `FoundationXML` only where it exists, and `_ = xmlParser.parse()` at five calls (the parser); `SourceNoteKit` only where it is a module of its own, which in the app it is not (the parser and the serializer); Markdown parsing only where Darwin exists, the paired-marker strip otherwise (`CitationPlainText`). `Linux/LinuxFoundationShims.swift` declares `String(localized:)` and `autoreleasepool` stand-ins only where Darwin and the Objective-C runtime are missing.
- **`Package.swift`**: `FRUSCoreKit` (path `FRUSCoreKit`, depending on `SourceNoteKit`) and `FRUSCoreKitTests` (path `FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit`): 39 library targets, 31 executables and 38 test targets. FRUS Explorer Light supplies `Crypto` on Linux in its own package.
- **The reader's path, in the kit** (`TEI/ReaderRendering.swift`, public): `ReaderLookups`, `ASTToRenderNodeConverter.init(readerOf:lookups:brokenRefs:)` and `FRUSRenderNodeHTMLSerializer.reader`, which `DocumentViewModel.load` and `HTMLTemplate.build` now call with what the app chooses. Access changes no symbol's name, and the app compiles these files into its own module.

The in-app citation suite is guarded test by test, so its caption rules and its check of the formatter's initializers run in both.
